editorial:
Imagine living in Brooklyn and getting caught in a messy love triangle with your weird neighbor and a girl who is fighting a lot of inner demons. You follow a graphic novelist who is trying to make it big, but his life gets complicated when he and his neighbor both fall for the same broken woman. It feels like a slow burn that captures that feeling of being young, lost, and trying to find where you fit in. The vibe is very raw and honest, focusing on how people deal with addiction and the fear of being left behind by the people they love.

You will probably love the acting because the emotions feel real and not forced. While the story moves a bit slow at times, it makes the emotional hits feel stronger. If you enjoy indie films that focus on character growth over big plot twists, you should definitely give this a try. It is a great pick for a rainy Sunday when you are in the mood for something thoughtful.
endingExplained: The story wraps up with the three characters finally facing their truth. Instead of a perfect happy ending, you see them accept that they cannot fix each other. The girl decides she needs to focus on her own healing and sobriety first. The two men realize their friendship is more stable than their romance. They all find a sense of peace by letting go of the idea of a traditional relationship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character studies and raw human stories.
